catalog.name: Precipitation
catalog.description: Global precipitation datasets including satellite-derived rainfall estimates and climate modeling products. These layers provide insights into rainfall patterns, drought monitoring, and hydrological analysis at various temporal scales.

members.name: CHIRPS v2.0 Monthly East
members.description: Dataset URL: https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS-2.0/

info.name: Background
info.content: CHIRPS provides rainfall estimates from rain gauge and satellite observations. Since 1999, USGS and CHC scientists—supported by USAID, NASA, and NOAA—have developed techniques for producing reliable rainfall maps for drought early warning and environmental monitoring.

info.name: Data Coverage
info.content: Quasi-global coverage spanning 50°S to 50°N with a temporal range from 1981 to near-present.

info.name: Methodology
info.content: Combines in-house climatology (CHPclim), 0.05° resolution satellite imagery, and interpolated station data to correct systematic biases from complex terrain.

info.name: Applications
info.content: Supports seasonal drought monitoring, trend analysis, and early warning systems such as FEWS NET.

info.name: More Information
info.content: Read more about CHIRPS

members.name: PERSIANN Monthly East
members.description: Dataset URL: https://chrsdata.eng.uci.edu/

info.name: Background
info.content: The PERSIANN (Precipitation Estimation from Remotely Sensed Information using Artificial Neural Networks) system was developed by the Center for Hydrometeorology and Remote Sensing (CHRS) at the University of California, Irvine (UCI). It uses neural network function classification/approximation procedures to compute estimates of rainfall rate from satellite imagery.

info.name: Data Coverage
info.content: The PERSIANN rainfall product covers 60°S to 60°N globally, with a spatial resolution of 0.25° x 0.25°.

info.name: Methodology
info.content: PERSIANN uses neural network function classification/approximation procedures to compute an estimate of rainfall rate at each 0.25° x 0.25° pixel of the infrared brightness temperature image provided by geostationary satellites. An adaptive training feature facilitates updating of the network parameters whenever independent estimates of rainfall are available.

info.name: Applications
info.content: PERSIANN data is widely used for climate studies, hydrological modeling, water resource management, and weather forecasting applications.

info.name: More Information
info.content: The PERSIANN system was initially based on geostationary infrared imagery and later extended to include the use of both infrared and daytime visible imagery. The algorithm used here is based on the geostationary longwave infrared imagery to generate global rainfall. Visit the CHRS Data Portal for more information

catalog.name: Rivers
catalog.description: Global river network datasets and hydrographic resources, including major river systems, drainage networks, and dam infrastructure. These layers support hydrological modeling, water resource management, and environmental studies.

members.name: Reservoirs by Country
members.description: The Global Dam Watch (GDW) Database provides a comprehensive, harmonized collection of over 35,000 reservoir polygons worldwide. Developed by the Global Dam Watch consortium, this database combines existing repositories with new data collected through citizen science, remote sensing, and machine learning. It includes all types of anthropogenic instream barriers, with priority given to major dams forming reservoirs and run-of-river barriers on larger waterways. This dataset is split by country for focused analysis and faster loading times.

members.name: HydroRIVERS
members.description: HydroRIVERS is a comprehensive global river network dataset containing 8.5 million individual river reaches with a total length of 35.9 million km. It includes all rivers with a catchment area of at least 10 km² or an average flow of at least 0.1 m³/sec. Extracted from the HydroSHEDS database at 15 arc-second resolution, each river segment contains key attributes including length, distance from headwaters and ocean outlets, river order, and estimated long-term average discharge. All reaches are co-registered with the HydroBASINS database through shared IDs, making it ideal for hydrological modeling and water resource management.

members.name: Hydrosheds Global 30s Void-filled DEM
members.description: Dataset URL: https://www.hydrosheds.org/hydrosheds-core-downloads

info.name: Background
info.content: The present data set demonstrates the potential of combining observed river discharge information with a climate-driven Water Balance Model to develop composite runoff fields that are consistent with observed discharges. These composite fields preserve the accuracy of the discharge measurements as well as the spatial and temporal distribution of simulated runoff, thereby providing the "best estimate" of terrestrial runoff over large domains.

info.name: Data Coverage
info.content: The dataset utilizes a gridded river network at 30-minute spatial resolution to represent riverine flow pathways, linking continental landmasses to the oceans. It integrates selected gauging stations from the Global Runoff Data Centre archive to ensure broad spatial coverage suitable for large-scale hydrological assessments.

info.name: Methodology
info.content: Selected gauging stations from the Global Runoff Data Centre archive were co-registered to a simulated topological network (STN-30p) developed at the University of New Hampshire. Inter-station regions along the STN-30p were identified, and inter-station discharge and runoff were calculated to compare observed values with outputs from the Water Balance Model simulation. Correction coefficients, based on the ratio of observed to simulated runoff in these areas, were then applied to create the composite runoff fields.

info.name: Applications
info.content: In addition to providing the composite runoff fields, the dataset includes intermediate products such as station attributes, long-term monthly runoff regimes of the selected gauging stations, the simulated topological network (STN-30p), and derived attributes for the stations. An HTML-based data explorer allows users to navigate the information from a global view down to subbasin or station-level details.

info.name: More Information
info.content: The printed version of the report can be ordered free of charge from GRDC (grdc@bafg.de) or WMO (dhwr@gateway.wmo.ch). Note: Due to inaccuracies in the topographical dataset used in compiling the simulated river network, graphical errors may occur for certain lower-order rivers. Users are encouraged to send their comments and error notifications to the provided email addresses.

info.content: In addition to providing the composite runoff fields, the dataset includes intermediate products such as station attributes, long-term monthly runoff regimes of the selected gauging stations, the simulated topological network (STN-30p), and derived attributes for the stations. An HTML-based data explorer allows users to navigate the information from a global view down to subbasin or station-level details.

info.name: More Information
info.content: The printed version of the report can be ordered free of charge from GRDC (grdc@bafg.de) or WMO (dhwr@gateway.wmo.ch). Note: Due to inaccuracies in the topographical dataset used in compiling the simulated river network, graphical errors may occur for certain lower-order rivers. Users are encouraged to send their comments and error notifications to the provided email addresses.
